record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: In Fe3GeTe2/FePS3, FePS3/Fe3GeTe2/FePS3, and Fe3GeTe2/MnPX3 (X = S, Se) heterostructures, how do oxidization of Fe3GeTe2, the type of antiferromagnetic ordering, interlayer coupling inside the antiferromagnet, reduced dimensionality, charge transfer, and possible interfacial spin reorientation control the enhanced magnetism and unusual exchange-bias behavior?

evidence.quote: Varying FePS3-thickness in such Fe3GeTe2/FePS3 heterostructures would also be essential to address the open questions regarding the effects of type of AFM ordering, interlayer coupling, and reduced dimensionality on the magnetism and EB behavior (the double-shifted hysteresis behavior).

Another effect that was not considered in the work [62] is "charge transfer" that could occur at the Fe3GeTe2/FePS3 interface and give rise to the enhanced magnetism and EB field in this heterostructure.

Nonetheless, the two-step magnetization versus temperature behavior observed around 100 K in the case of MnPSe3 remains questionable as a re-orientation of spins at the Fe3GeTe2/MnPSe3 interface may occur around this temperature. This hypothesis must be examined and validated experimentally.

There are also open questions about the effects of oxidization (the oxidized Fe3GeTe2 layer), interlayer coupling within the AFM layer, charge-transfer across the Fe3GeTe2/MnPX3 (X = S, Se) interface, and the effects of reduced dimensionality on the magnetism of Fe3GeTe2 and hence the EB effect observed in these heterostructures [18].

artifact.category_tag: van der Waals magnetic heterostructures and exchange bias
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a set of open questions about the microscopic origin of enhanced magnetism and exchange bias in FGT/FePS3 and FGT/MnPX3 heterostructures. Recent literature (2022–2025) on FGT-based 2D vdW heterostructures continues to investigate EB, interfacial charge transfer, and oxidation effects, but no comprehensive model disentangling all listed mechanisms has been established. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Open questions about oxidation, AFM ordering, interlayer coupling, reduced dimensionality, charge transfer, and interfacial spin reorientation in FGT/FePS3 and FGT/MnPX3 heterostructures.
status_evidence.claim: The listed mechanisms are explicitly identified as open questions for these heterostructures.
